Title 1:
The Baseline Ratio of Neutrophils to Lymphocytes Is Associated with Patient Prognosis in Advanced Gastric Cancer
Abstract 1:
Objective : In cancer patients , the balance between neutrophil ( N ) and lymphocyte ( L ) cell counts fluctuates with advancing disease . The objective of our study was to determine the prognostic implication s of the N/L ratio in the peripheral blood of gastric cancer patients . Methods : Study participants were identified from a prospect i ve cohort of patients with advanced gastric cancer in Japan ( n = 1,220 ) . Results : The median baseline N/L was 2.58 ( range , 0.63–12.7 ) . Univariate analysis revealed that patients with an N/L ≧2.5 ( n = 644 ) had a significantly poorer prognosis than those with an N/L < 2.5 ( n = 576 ; log rank test , p = 0.019 × 10–12 ) . The median survival times for these two groups were 239 ( 95 % confidence interval , CI , 217–251 days ) and 363 days ( 95 % CI , 334–406 days ) , respectively , while the 1-year survival rates were 30 ( 95 % CI , 26–34 % ) and 50 % ( 95 % CI , 45–54 % ) , respectively . A multivariate Cox model established a significant relationship between the N/L ratio and survival ( adjusted hazard ratio = 1.52 ; 95 % CI , 1.32–1.75 ; p = 0.077 × 10–8 ) . Conclusions : These results suggest that the N/L ratio is an independent prognostic factor in advanced gastric cancer . Measurement of this ratio may serve as a clinical ly accessible and useful biomarker for patient survival


Title 2:
Validation of the prognostic relevance of plasma C-reactive protein levels in soft-tissue sarcoma patients
Abstract 2:
Background : The concept of the involvement of systemic inflammation in cancer progression and metastases has gained attraction within the past decade . C-reactive protein ( CRP ) , a non-specific blood-based marker of the systemic inflammatory response , has been associated with decreased survival in several cancer types . The aim of the present study was to vali date the prognostic value of pre-operative plasma CRP levels on clinical outcome in a large cohort of soft-tissue sarcoma ( STS ) patients . Methods : Three hundred and four STS patients , operated between 1998 and 2010 , were retrospectively evaluated .  CRP levels and the impact on cancer-specific survival ( CSS ) , disease-free survival ( DFS ) and overall survival ( OS ) were assessed using Kaplan – Meier curves and univariate as well as multivariate Cox proportional models . Additionally , we developed a nomogram by supplementing the plasma CRP level to the well-established Kattan nomogram and evaluated the improvement of predictive accuracy of this novel nomogram by applying calibration and Harrell ’s concordance index ( c-index ) . Results : An elevated plasma CRP level was significantly associated with established prognostic factors , including age , tumour grade , size and depth ( P<0.05 ) . In multivariate analysis , increased CRP levels were significantly associated with a poor outcome for CSS ( HR=2.05 ; 95 % CI=1.13–3.74 ; P=0.019 ) and DFS ( HR=1.88 ; 95 % CI=1.07–3.34 ; P=0.029 ) . The estimated c-index was 0.74 using the original Kattan nomogram and 0.77 when the plasma CRP level was added . Conclusion : An elevated pre-operative CRP level represents an independent prognostic factor that predicts poor prognosis and improves the predictive ability of the Kattan nomogram in STS patients . Our data suggest to further prospect ively vali date its potential utility for individual risk stratification and clinical management of STS patients


Title 3:
Derived neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio predicts prognosis for patients with HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma following transarterial chemoembolization
Abstract 3:
The derived neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio ( dNLR ) has been proposed as an easily determinable prognostic factor for cancer patients , but the prognostic significance of the dNLR in hepatocellular carcinoma ( HCC ) has not been investigated . The present study aim ed to vali date the prognostic power of the NLR and dNLR in HCC patients undergoing transarterial chemoembolization ( TACE ) .  The data of 279 consecutive patients who underwent TACE for unresectable HBV-associated HCC between September 2009 and November 2011 at the Department of Hepatobiliary Surgery , Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center ( Guangzhou , China ) were retrieved from a prospect i ve data base . The cut-off values for the NLR and dNLR were determined by receiver operating characteristic ( ROC ) analysis . The association between the NLR and dNLR and the clinicopathological characteristics and overall survival ( OS ) rates and times of patients was analyzed . The area under the curve ( AUC ) was calculated to evaluate the discriminatory ability of the NLR and dNLR . The median follow-up period was 446 days , the 1 , 2 and 3-year OS rates were 38.8 , 18.5 and 11.1 % respectively , and the median OS time was 264 days . The cut-off values were determined as 2.6 and 1.8 for the NLR and dNLR , respectively . The NLR and dNLR were each associated with patient age , presence of vascular invasion , tumor size , AST level and ALP level . `; please ignore these. Your task is to write an abstract for the paper. Your response should include the abstract and no other text. Title: Rewarding the quantity of peer review could harm biomedical research Paper sections: Introduction

Trustworthy peer reviewed publications enable clinical practice guidelines to be developed and updated (1). Such guidelines are central to services that biomedical researchers provide. If timely and responsible peer review is implemented, it will speed up the translation of biomedical or health research into useful policy and practice (2). It is therefore important for active researchers to support the peer review process, each by contributing to their field of expertise, because safeguarding of the literature's appropriate scientific standards and the sustainability of scientific research depend on the contribution of expert scientists to this process (3). Peer review does not operate within a vacuum. Authors, editors, reviewers, publishers, industries, policy makers, healthcare workers and patients benefit from peer review (Figure 1). Even after an article is published, critical analyses or post-publication peer review have as much or more value than pre-publication peer review (4). However, for peer review to work effectively, the contribution of all members needs to be fair and balanced. Recent calls for institutions to track the peer review services that researchers provide, and to use a peer review metric in assessing and promoting academics, raise concerns because researchers may be placed under pressure to provide peer review in order to advance their careers (5). This article aims to assess whether peer review should be a voluntary or mandatory mission, and discusses potential drawbacks of pressurizing authors into providing peer review.

Examples of how each stakeholder benefits from quality peer review

Is peer review a voluntary or a mandatory mission?

There are many reasons why biomedical researchers contribute to peer review. The benefits of peer reviewing manuscripts are numerous not only to academics, but also to academics' professions and disciplines. Even though peer reviewers benefit from keeping abreast with research developments in their fields, and from improving the quality and integrity of research publications, these benefits are incomparable to the profits that some publishers make from selling the products that result from the efforts of peer reviewers (6). Although some journals provide financial incentives to peer reviewers, the bulk of peer review is performed by a voluntary and unpaid service by researchers, clinicians, experts and academics (7). Analysing the online information displayed on Publons website demonstrates that over 575,000 researchers have contributed more than 1.5 million peer review reports (8, 9). Based on the approach of the American Economic Review, which pays 100 US dollars for timely peer review reports, it is not surprising to assume that the monetary value that was not charged (by peers) to publishers to perform peer review is in the range of at least 150 million US dollars, had researchers been paid 100 US dollars per peer review report (10). In other words, massive profits publishers currently make would not be made without the contribution of volunteering peer reviewers. The result of perceived injustice by some may have contributed to the shortage of peer reviewers, so that finding suitable reviewers with sufficient experience and skills has become a challenging and time-consuming task. Interestingly, Heinemann the editor of Journal of Diabetes Science and Technology, a SAGE journal, raised the issue of whether a reviewer was an "endangered species" (11). One solution to finding peer reviewers was to establish a database of reviewers, and to consider options that would allow the recognition of peer review to attract more peer reviewers to the process of validating scientific publications (12-14). One has to wonder why this had not occurred to all stakeholders of the publishing process prior to 2014-2016. The idea of providing meaningful recognition for peer review activity is encouraged and is long overdue, but it can be argued that pressuring or inducing academics to provide peer review services is likely to result in questionable practices, practices that are likely to impair the quality of published biomedical research because if the process is forced and is not natural, it could lead to the creation of perverse incentives (15).

Potential drawbacks to pressured or induced peer review

Herman remarked that "the moral status of an action is connected to an agent's judgment and choice" (16). Thus, if academics are forced or pressurized to peer review to receive extra points and pad their portfolios with peer review reports, it will lead to an increase in the number of peer reviewers, but will not necessarily lead to improving the quality of peer review. This outcome is likely, as demonstrated by Fiala and Willett, who showed that the "quality" of publications, as measured by the Clarivate AnalyticsTM journal impact factor (JIF), was not accompanied by a substantial increase in the rate of publications (17). When they averaged the JIF, they found that the mean JIF dropped from 1.455 for 1989-2000 and to 1.302 for 2001-2014 (17).

Another disadvantage of pressuring academics to perform peer review may lead to increased competition between academics so that the number of academics chasing peer review in order to pad their curriculum vitae is likely to increase. If such a demand is not provided by reputable journals, some academics, under pressure of their job requirement, will have no option but to provide services to an increasing market of unscholarly or "predatory" journals or publishers in order to fulfil this enforced requirement. By providing pressured peer review to "predatory" journals, reviewers would in essence provide a mask of legitimate peer review to journals with questionable publishing practices. Needless to say that such journals, under increasing pressure, need to provide "any, even if meaningless" peer review to improve their image and justify their article processing charges, although it could then be argued that if they provide legitimate peer review, then they are not "predatory" journals. The issue is a grey area since fake peer reviews plague both "predatory" journals as well as indexed journals that are traditionally considered to be safe.

Juxtaposing the current model of “rewarding peer review” with “publish or perish”

The Publons model, which offers academics recognition for their activity in providing peer review, and rewards them for the number of peer review reports, should not ignore the fact that peer review has been and should remain a voluntary task (18, 19). If this model is misused, it may pressurize authors. In other words, if peer review becomes a mandatory requirement for tenure, the threat of job loss is likely to jeopardize academics' (i.e., peer reviewers') free will, and add a layer of pressure. Arguably, pressurized peer reviewers are unlikely to improve the quality of peer review. Early manifestations of the "publish or perish" mandate made publications a mandatory requirement for tenure in many countries (20). There are signs that the Publons model is using marketing strategies that can be misused and could expose academics to the risks of coercion (21). The Publons model was used by three journals that appointed a dog to their editorial boards in a sting by Professor Mike Daube, a public health expert in Perth, Australia: EC Pulmonology and Respiratory Medicine, Journal of Community Medicine and Public Health Care and Journal of Tobacco Stimulated Diseases (22-25). Pressure to peer review may lead to consequences that are similar to those witnessed in the publish or perish culture and its association with research misconduct such as paying fake peer reviewers or exploiting non-expert junior researchers who are less likely to provide critical peer review or carefully scrutinize manuscripts before they are published (26).

The pressure to peer review is similar to the pressure to publish, and the latter has led to publication bias and compromised the objectivity and integrity of research (27). Although these strategies discussed above are used in good faith to encourage academics to contribute to peer review, they include messages that could lead to implementing a criterion of peer review by promotion and tenure committees, or to adding another perverse incentive (28). Furthermore, readers are urged to consider who may be targeted by a recommendation to include a verified peer review record when seeking a visa or Green Card in the United States of America (29). A computational materials scientist at the University of Florida, who had secured his Green Card for the United States of America, shared with Publons how he used statistics on his Publons Verifiable Review Record, offered tips on how to use peer review to boost Green Card applications, and advised researchers to make their peer review public.

Publons awards the number of papers that have been peer reviewed by displaying the number of verified reviews, the number of reviews in the last six months, and the number of verified editors record for each reviewer. Thus, quantifying peer review activity may be erroneous and unfair to experts in a niche field because they are likely to receive very few invitations to peer review by virtue of the fact that very few articles are published in their narrow field. Conversely, a researcher who is one of few experts in a rather popular field may get more review invitations because there are not many reviewers available in that field.

It should be cautioned that the competition between peer reviewers striving to boost their Publons profiles with more and more reports might increase peer review fraud, or dishonesty, or at least compromise the quality of peer review and its products. Altman remarked that the pressure to publish created a temptation to behave dishonestly when "all too often the main reason for a piece of research seems to be to lengthen a researcher's curriculum vitae" (30). With Altman's statement in mind and given the gradual increasing transition to open access and the inevitable explosion of journals, can biomedical researchers bear the consequences of being further pressurized into showing a lengthy peer review record as evidence of scholarly contribution or productivity?

Conclusion

Pressuring or inducing academics into creating a list of peer review reports raises serious questions about the quality of such peer review and the value that such an action adds to biomedical research. To encourage researchers to participate in efficient peer review, we recommend eliminating sources of pressure, preventing violations of researchers' rights, protecting vulnerable early career researchers from being pressured or induced into providing non-expert peer review, and encouraging and rewarding quality voluntary peer review (31, 32). Rewarding reviewers who provide quality peer review can be achieved by paying peer reviewers for their time and expertise. The adoption of an open peer-review system wherein experts engage in validating and grading peer review according to specific guidelines for each scientific field is feasible (33). Finally, promoting a sense of shared responsibility, and encouraging experts to provide post publication peer review, is likely to weed out poor reviewers, and instil a culture of responsible peer review of biomedical research.

Potential conflict of interest: None declared.

Voluntary peer review is generally provided by researchers as a duty or service to their disciplines. They commit their expertise, knowledge and time freely without expecting rewards or compensation. Peer review can be perceived as a reciprocal mission that aims to safeguard the quality of publications by helping authors improve their manuscripts. While voluntary peer review adds value to research, rewarding the quantity or the volume of peer review is likely to lure academics into providing poor quality peer review. Consequently, the quantity of peer review may increase, but at the expense of quality, which may lead to unintended consequences and might negatively affect the quality of biomedical publications. This paper aims to present evidence that while voluntary peer review may aid researchers, pressurized peer review may create a perverse incentive that negatively affects the integrity of the biomedical research record. We closely examine one of the proposed models for rewarding peer review based on the quantity of peer review reports. This article also argues that peer review should remain a voluntary mission, and should not be prompted by the need to attain tenure or promotion.

Abstract:

Abrasive wear on eroded root dentine after different periods of exposure to saliva in situ . The effect of salivary exposure time on the abrasive wear of acid-eroded dentine was evaluated in situ . One-hundred and twenty bovine root dentine slabs were randomly assigned into six groups ( A-F ) and placed in intraoral palatal devices , which were worn by 10 volunteers for 4 d. On the first day , no erosive/abrasive procedures were carried out . On the following 3 d , erosive challenges were performed extraorally , two times per day , by immersing the device for 90 s in a soft drink . Subsequently , the group A specimens were immediately brushed ( 40 strokes ) , and the others were brushed after the following times : B , 20 min ; C , 40 min ; and D , 60 min . Group E specimens were only acid-eroded and those of group F were only brushed . Dentine wear was measured with a profilometer . anova and Dunnett 's test showed that groups A-D did not differ statistically from the control group E but differed from the control group F. The lowest mean value was found for group F. Regression analysis was unable to show salivary effect on dentine wear reduction . The data suggest that the exposure time of saliva of up to 60 min has no effect on reducing the eroded dentine wear by toothbrushing .

Abstract:

What should we do about student use of cognitive enhancers? An analysis of current evidence. This article reviews current data on the use of cognition enhancers as study aids in the student population. It identifies gaps and uncertainties in the knowledge required to make a balanced assessment of the need for some form of regulation. The review highlights the weak evidence on the prevalence of use of such drugs, especially outside the US, and the ambiguous evidence for their efficacy in a healthy population. Risks are well documented for the commonly used drugs, but poorly appreciated by users. These include not only the side-effects of the drugs themselves, but risks associated with on-line purchase, which offers no guarantees of authenticity and which for some drugs is illegal. The case for urgent action to regulate use is often linked to the belief that new and more effective drugs are likely to appear in the near future. The evidence for this is weak. However, drugs are not the only possible route to neuroenhancement and action is needed to collect more data on the impact of existing drugs, as well as new technologies, in order to guide society in making a proportionate response to the issue. This article is part of a Special Issue entitled 'Cognitive Enhancers'.

What is IIIF ?

IIIF stands for International Image Interoperability Framework. It is a set of open standards developed to enable the rich, high-quality sharing, comparison, and annotation of images on the web. IIIF is designed to give scholars, researchers, and other users the ability to access and interact with high-resolution image resources held in different institutions and repositories in a consistent and powerful way.

IIIF focuses on the delivery and presentation of images, providing a way to retrieve and view images through a common protocol, which includes standardized URLs for requesting image content. This allows developers to create image viewers and other tools that can work with any image server that supports IIIF, without needing to adapt to different APIs or data models.

The main components of IIIF include:

1. Image API: This is a RESTful web service that allows for the dynamic request of images and the properties of those images. It includes parameters for size, rotation, quality, format, and region of interest, which allows for the manipulation of images on-the-fly.

2. Presentation API: It provides information needed to allow a client to present and navigate the structure and layout of complex image-based objects, such as manuscripts, maps, books, and other visual materials.

3. Search API: This allows for a more straightforward search within the text of images, such as pages of books with annotations or transcriptions.

4. Authentication API: Designed to provide a standardized mechanism for controlled access to resources, accommodating the reality that not all IIIF resources are openly available to the public.

IIIF's ability to standardize how images are requested and delivered has made it a significant tool for cultural heritage and academic institutions, enabling them to share their image collections with a wide audience and allow users to work with the digital representations in versatile and meaningful ways.

can you set a large page file for memory intensive tasks?

Yes, you can set a large page file (also known as a swap file or virtual memory) to help manage memory-intensive tasks on a computer, especially when the physical RAM (Random Access Memory) is fully utilized or limited.

The page file acts as an extension of the physical RAM, allowing the operating system to move less frequently accessed data from the RAM to the page file on the hard disk or SSD (Solid State Drive). This process frees up RAM for more immediate tasks and can improve performance for memory-intensive applications, albeit at the cost of slower access times compared to direct RAM access due to the slower nature of storage devices compared to RAM.

Here's how you can set or adjust the page file size in Windows (as an example):

1. **Right-click** on **This PC** or **My Computer** on the desktop or in File Explorer, then select **Properties**.
2. Click on **Advanced system settings** on the left side.
3. In the **System Properties** window, go to the **Advanced** tab.
4. Under **Performance**, click **Settings**.
5. Go to the **Advanced** tab in the Performance Options window.
6. Under **Virtual memory**, click **Change**.
7. Uncheck **Automatically manage paging file size for all drives**.
8. Select the drive where the page file is located (commonly the C: drive).
9. Click the option **Custom size**, and then enter the desired **Initial size (MB)** and **Maximum size (MB)** for your page file. It's a common practice to set the initial size and maximum size to the same value to prevent the page file from fragmenting.
10. Click **Set**, then **OK** and **Apply** the changes. You may be required to restart your computer for the changes to take effect.

When setting the size of your page file, a common recommendation is to have it 1.5 to 3 times the size of your physical RAM, though this can vary based on your specific usage, total available disk space, and the amount of RAM in your system. For very memory-intensive tasks, or if you encounter errors indicating that your system is low on memory, you might opt to increase the page file size beyond this recommendation.

It's important to note that relying too much on the page file can lead to performance issues since accessing data from a disk is significantly slower than accessing data from RAM. Therefore, for the best performance with memory-intensive tasks, it's also advisable to physically add more RAM to your system if possible.

### Question 1
How can you correctly initialize an array in JavaScript with the values 1, 2, and 3?

A. `let arr = 1, 2, 3;`  
B. `let arr = array(1, 2, 3);`  
C. `let arr = [1, 2, 3];`  
D. `let arr = newArray(1, 2, 3);`

**Correct Response:** C. `let arr = [1, 2, 3];`

**Explanation of the Correct Answer:**
The correct way to initialize an array in JavaScript with specific values (1, 2, and 3, in this case) is by using square brackets `[]` with the values separated by commas within the brackets, as shown in option C. This is the most common and straightforward way to create an array in JavaScript.

**Tip:** Remember, in JavaScript, arrays can be created using square brackets `[]`, and they can hold multiple values of different types.

---

### Question 2
What is the result of the following code snippet if you want to set the value at index 1 of the array `arr` to 4?

```javascript
let arr = [1, 2, 3];
arr[1] = 4;
console.log(arr);
```

A. `[1, 2, 3]`  
B. `[1, 4, 3]`  
C. `[4, 2, 3]`  
D. Error

**Correct Response:** B. `[1, 4, 3]`

**Explanation of the Correct Answer:**
When you access an array element using its index (with the first index being 0), you can directly set its value. In the code snippet, `arr[1] = 4;` changes the value of the second element (at index 1) of the array `arr` from 2 to 4. Thus, when printed, `arr` has been modified to `[1, 4, 3]`.

**Tip:** Remember, array indices in JavaScript start at 0. Directly setting a value to an array index updates that element with the new value.

Modifying an element directly by its index, as shown in options B and D, are also correct approaches.

Loss function

A loss function, also known as a cost function or objective function, is a crucial concept in machine learning, statistics, and optimization. It measures the difference or error between the expected or true outcome and the outcome predicted by a model. The primary goal of most learning algorithms is to minimize the loss function, thereby improving the model’s accuracy in making predictions or decisions.

There are various types of loss functions, each designed for specific types of problems. The choice of a loss function depends on the task (e.g., classification, regression) and the specific characteristics of the data:

1. **Mean Squared Error (MSE)**: Used for regression problems. It calculates the square of the difference between actual values and the predictions. It's given by the formula: \(MSE = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N (y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2\), where \(N\) is the number of samples, \(y_i\) the actual value, and \(\hat{y}_i\) the predicted value.
   
2. **Mean Absolute Error (MAE)**: Also used for regression. It calculates the absolute difference between actual values and predictions, making it less sensitive to outliers than MSE. The formula is: \(MAE = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N | y_i - \hat{y}_i |\).

3. **Cross-Entropy Loss (Log Loss)**: Commonly used in classification problems, especially for binary classification. It measures the performance of a classification model whose output is a probability value between 0 and 1. The loss increases as the predicted probability diverges from the actual label.

    - For binary classification: \(- \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N [y_i \log(\hat{y}_i) + (1 - y_i) \log(1 - \hat{y}_i)]\)
    - For multi-class classification, it's called categorical cross-entropy.

4. **Hinge Loss**: Widely used for support vector machines and some types of neural networks in classification tasks, especially with the intention of creating a margin between classes. It is defined as: \( \max(0, 1 - y_i \cdot \hat{y}_i)\), where \(y_i\) is the actual class label (-1 or 1 in binary classification) and \(\hat{y}_i\) is the predicted value.

5. **Huber Loss**: Combines elements of MSE and MAE, being quadratic for small errors (making it smooth and differentiable, like MSE) and linear for larger errors (reducing sensitivity to outliers, like MAE). It is defined by a parameter \(\delta\) which dictates the transition between the two:

    \[
    L_{\delta}(a) = 
    \begin{cases} 
    \frac{1}{2}a^2 & \text{for } |a| \leq \delta \\
    \delta (|a| - \frac{1}{2}\delta) & \text{otherwise}
    \end{cases}
    \]
    
    where \(a = y - \hat{y}\).

Choosing the right loss function is vital for training effective models. It influences how the models learn and evolve during the training process. The optimization algorithms adjust the model parameters (e.g., weights in a neural network) to minimize the loss function value across the training dataset, aiming to improve model predictions.

INT. SÉVERINE'S ART STUDIO - DAY

Background: 
The sun pours in through high windows illuminating every corner of SÉVERINE'S spacious art studio, an eclectic mix of colorful canvases and clay sculptures. Charcoal sketches are tacked to the walls, and paintbrushes are scattered carelessly around. CLÉMENTINE, Séverine's quirky childhood friend and fellow artist, has come over to help Séverine find inspiration for an avant-garde art competition. Séverine has been so engrossed in her work that she's ignored all urges and rational thought about basic needs.

CHARACTERS:

SÉVERINE - late 20s, an intense and eccentric artist with shoulder-length, untamed auburn hair. She dons a large, paint-splattered white T-shirt over relaxed, olive-green cargo shorts that are loose but filled with tools and brushes. She's barefoot, her toes stained with various paint colors.

CLÉMENTINE - early 30s, an earthy, vibrant soul with tightly curled brunette hair, wearing a flowing patterned blouse and snug, high-waisted flared jeans. A pair of vintage red cat-eye glasses perch on her nose.

Séverine is pacing frantically, her face contorted in discomfort. Clémentine observes her with an arched eyebrow, trying to understand her friend's behavior.

SÉVERINE
(breathless)
Clementine, je te jure, if I don't channel my inner Picasso soon, je vais exploser!

CLÉMENTINE
(cheerfully)
Alors, let's find that inner masterpiece, mon amie. We'll start with stark contrasts – life and death, love and holiness! 

Clémentine energetically sweeps a brush loaded with black paint across a white canvas when suddenly, Séverine clutches her stomach, face reddening.

CLÉMENTINE (CONT'D)
(cautiously)
Séverine, are you sure you're feeling bien? You look a little... green.

SÉVERINE
(wincing)
No, no, it's nothing. Focus, Séverine, focus. Just... Nervous for the competition, c'est tout.

Séverine tries to resume painting, but her hand shakes, sending a line of paint cascading down the canvas. Clémentine watches, confused.

SÉVERINE (CONT'D)
(urgently)
Excuse-moi, Clem, I need un moment de solitude.

Clémentine nods in understanding, thinking Séverine needs a spark of inspiration. Séverine turns her back to Clémentine, and with trembling hands, she reaches behind her back, fumbling with something at her waist.

CLÉMENTINE
(concern growing)
Séverine... what are you doing?

A distinct and discomforting NOISE fills the room, followed by Séverine's mortified expression. Her cargo shorts visibly expand around the rear area. Séverine stands frozen, an absurd stance of defeat.

SÉVERINE
(horrified whisper)
Mon Dieu. Ça s'est vraiment passé.

Clémentine gapes before bursting into laughter, doubling over while the initial shock fades into ridiculous reality.

CLÉMENTINE
(teasing)
Mais, Séverine, tu as peint un chef-d'oeuvre dans ton pantalon!

SÉVERINE
(embarrassed, defensive)
Arrête! It's this damn competition! I was so absorbed, I – I forgot...

CLÉMENTINE
(still laughing)
Oublié? Séverine, how could you forget, chérie? The human body has its limits!

Séverine tries to sidestep away, attempting to preserve her dignity. Clémentine's nose wrinkles as the smell reaches her.

SÉVERINE
(miserable)
S'il te plaît, Clem. It was an accident! An artistic sacrifice!

CLÉMENTINE
(mocking)
Ah oui? A sacrifice? More like a surrender to nature! 

Séverine looks down at her soiled shorts, the gravity of the situation sinking in. She attempts to crack a smile.

SÉVERINE
(trying to stay light-hearted)
C'est ma nouvelle forme d'expression. The 'fecal realism' period, perhaps?

CLÉMENTINE
(playfully)
Realism? That's rich. Let's call it 'abstract expressionism', because that, my friend, looks like an emotional outburst. 

Séverine scowls as Clémentine continues to wave her hand in front of her face, dramatizing her disgust.

SÉVERINE
(ashamed)
Alright, alright. I've made mon point... quite graphically.

Clémentine goes to the window and opens it, letting the fresh air sweep into the studio.

CLÉMENTINE
(playfully authoritative)
Well, Madame Picasso, let's get you cleaned up. The only aroma I want in this studio is the scent of fresh paint and triumph, not... this.

Séverine chuckles in spite of herself, accepting the hand Clémentine offers. 

SÉVERINE
(sincerely grateful)
Merci, Clem. Je ne sais pas ce que je ferais sans toi.

CLÉMENTINE
(grinning)
Evidemment, who else would brave the stench of defeat with you? Now, marchons – to the shower with you. And afterward, we paint!

They link arms, the dialogue turning to playful banter as they exit, leaving the soiled shorts and Séverine's embarrassment behind in favor of friendship and laughter.

As the golden rays of the morning sun pierced through the lavish draperies of the Emperor's private chambers, the Roman leader, hardened by countless battles and political maneuverings, stood as a titan among mortals. Beside him, within the opulence of silken sheets, lay the delicate figure of a young Germanic captive, spared from death in the sand and blood-stained arena of the Colosseum. His fair hair spilled over the plush pillows like streams of molten gold and his body, though bearing the lean robustness of the warrior he too was, contrasted sharply with the burly form of the Emperor. Despite having been plucked from the churning chaos of gladiatorial combat, the young man, named Aric, seemed unfazed as he lounged au naturel, indulging in a spread of figs, honeyed wine, and various delicacies. 

Emperor Gaius watched him with a hawkish eye, a curious fondness growing where he least expected it. The Germanic youth had fought with a ferocity that belied his graceful appearance, and it was this blend of beauty and resilience that had stayed the emperor's hand when he could have easily condemned the boy to death with a simple thumb turned downwards.

"My dear Aric," Gaius began, his voice an intriguing mix of omnipotence and vulnerability, "You have stolen the breath from my chest, not by the sword or spear, but by a force far more cunning. Fate has thrown us together in such tumultuous times, yet here we are, speaking candidly beyond the vista of Rome."

Aric, unabashed by his nudity, simply plucked another fig from the bowl and bit into it, the sweetness overflowing onto his lips. He turned his arresting blue gaze upon the most powerful man in the known world and considered his proposition. "You would have me, a vanquished foe, as more than a trophy—more than a spoil of war?" Aric inquired, setting the fruit aside, his voice quietly defiant, lustrous with the hint of an afterglow from his recent brush with death.

what binds first transcription factors or rna polymerase

In the process of gene transcription in eukaryotic cells, transcription factors generally bind to specific regions of the DNA first. They recognize and attach to promoter regions or other regulatory sequences near the gene that is to be transcribed. Each transcription factor can serve a unique role, such as helping to recruit the RNA polymerase, altering the chromatin structure, or mediating interactions with other transcription factors and co-activators to form a pre-initiation complex (PIC).

RNA polymerase II, which is responsible for transcribing mRNA from DNA, typically binds to the promoter DNA after various transcription factors are already in place. The most well-known of these transcription factors is TFIID, which contains the TATA-binding protein (TBP) that recognizes and binds to the TATA box (if present) in the promoter region. This interaction is often the first step in the formation of the PIC. Subsequently, other general transcription factors and RNA polymerase II assemble at the promoter, with the help of mediator complexes if needed.

Once the PIC is fully assembled, the RNA polymerase II is properly positioned to begin RNA synthesis from the DNA template. This sequence of events ensures the controlled and specific expression of genes, as directed by the combination of transcription factors present in a particular cell type at a given time under specific physiological conditions.

오마카세 식사 경험은 단순히 음식을 먹는 것을 넘어서고, 셰프의 장인정신, 창의성, 그리고 재료에 대한 깊은 존중을 경험하는 것입니다. 셰프는 각 손님의 취향과 식사 속도를 세심하게 고려하여 개별 맞춤형 서비스를 제공하며, 때때로 그 자리에서 생선을 손질하거나 음식을 조리하는 과정을 고객에게 직접 보여 주기도 합니다.

오마카세는 다음과 같은 특징을 갖습니다:

1. 신선함: 재료는 가장 신선한 상태에서 바로 손님에게 제공되어, 전형적으로 그날의 시장에서 공수한 최상의 생선이나 채소가 사용됩니다.

游戏的主题探讨了公正、自由、社会改革等重要话题。玩家将探索各种地点，与游戏角色互动，并通过回合制战斗系统与敌人战斗。游戏也包含了养成元素，如角色间的友谊和浪漫关系的发展。

《女神异闻录5》因其独特的艺术风格、吸引人的故事和深度的角色发展得到了广泛的好评。游戏的成功导致了一系列衍生作品的发展，包括动画系列、漫画和改编游戏。

2019年，《女神异闻录5》发布了一个扩展版本《女神异闻录5 皇家版》（Persona 5 Royal），加入了新的故事内容、新的角色和改进的游戏机制。这一版本进一步深化了原有剧情，增加了更多的探索元素和养成要素，使得这款已经备受好评的游戏更加完善。

A super node contains a voltage source between two meshes, a grounded voltage source, a non grounded voltage source, or a current source between 2 meshes?

In the context of circuit analysis, a super node is a conceptual tool used when applying mesh analysis or nodal analysis to circuits that contain voltage sources, including dependent or independent sources.

A super node is created when:

1. **A voltage source between two non-reference nodes (meshes):** When a voltage source is connected to two non-reference nodes in a circuit, it constrains the voltage difference between those two nodes to a fixed value. In nodal analysis, these two nodes are treated as a single extended node or "super node." This allows us to write a single node voltage equation that incorporates both nodes and the voltage source between them.

2. **A grounded voltage source:** If you have a voltage source connected directly to a reference node (ground), this does not create a super node. Instead, you have a clear definition for the voltage at the non-reference node. However, if there are other elements or sources connected to the same node, it might influence how you consider the overall analysis.

3. **A non-grounded voltage source:** This refers to a voltage source that is not connected to a reference node. In most cases, this scenario would imply the voltage source is in series with components connected to two different non-reference nodes, which would then be incorporated into a super node if you are using nodal analysis.

4. **A current source between 2 meshes:** The presence of a current source between two meshes does not necessitate the creation of a super node. In fact, current sources are usually handled differently than voltage sources when performing mesh analysis. With a current source, the current is known, and this fact is used in creating the mesh equations. However, in nodal analysis, if a current source is connected between two non-reference nodes, it impacts the nodal equations for the two nodes it connects but does not create a super node.

Out of the options you've listed, the one that typically results in the formation of a super node is a voltage source between two non-reference nodes (meshes). With the super node concept, you account for the voltage source in nodal analysis by writing an equation that encompasses both nodes and the voltage between them, effectively treating them as a single extended node.

2. **Варварские племена налётчиков**: Здесь подойдет **Королевство Норвегия** (*Regnum Norwegiæ*), в период викингов, известных своими морскими набегами и завоеваниями.

6. **Некрополь нежити и некромантов**: Для данной фракции аналогии в исторических государствах найти сложнее, но можно вспомнить о **Лесах Арденн** (*Arduenna Silva*), месте, окруженное множеством мифов и легенд, что может ассоциироваться с наличием потусторонних сил.

7. **Демоническая армия разорения**: Исторические противники часто демонизировали врагов, можно ассоциировать с **Монгольской империей** (*Mongolyn Ezent Güren*), которая не как не вписывается в территориальные рамки современной Европы, но восприятие ее военных походов в Европе исключительно как разорения и подчинения можно абстрактно использовать.

Comment Nagios fait pour récupérer des metrics sur mes différents backends ?

Nagios utilise plusieurs mécanismes pour récupérer des métriques de différents backends ou systèmes surveillés. Voici comment il fonctionne généralement :

1. **NRPE (Nagios Remote Plugin Executor) :** C'est l'un des moyens les plus courants de surveiller des ressources à distance. Sur la machine distante que vous souhaitez surveiller, vous installez le démon NRPE. Nagios interroge ensuite le démon NRPE sur la machine distante, qui exécute en retour des plugins locaux pour vérifier l'état des ressources locales, telles que la charge du processeur, l'utilisation de la mémoire, l'espace disque, etc. NRPE récupère ces informations et les renvoie à la machine Nagios.

2. **NSClient++ pour les systèmes Windows :** Un agent similaire à NRPE mais destiné aux systèmes Windows. Il est installé sur l’host Windows et peut exécuter différents checks localement et retourner les résultats à Nagios.

3. **SSH :** Nagios peut exécuter des commandes à distance via SSH pour récupérer des métriques sur des systèmes Unix/Linux. Ce mécanisme est souvent utilisé si NRPE n’est pas une option ou pour des raisons de sécurité où SSH est préféré.

4. **SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol) :** Nagios peut également utiliser SNMP pour interroger les périphériques réseau (comme les commutateurs, les routeurs) et d'autres appareils prenant en charge SNMP (comme les imprimantes, les NAS, etc.) pour collecter des métriques.

5. **Check Plugins :** Ce sont les scripts exécutés par Nagios (ou par NRPE/NSClient++ en son nom) pour effectuer des contrôles spécifiques. Les plugins peuvent être écrits dans presque n'importe quel langage de programmation et sont conçus pour retourner un statut et, éventuellement, une sortie contenant des informations ou des métriques spécifiques.

6. **Passive Checks :** Nagios peut accepter des métriques et des informations d'état envoyées par des sources extérieures. Ces mécanismes sont utilisés pour les systèmes qui ne peuvent pas être interrogés activement par Nagios ou pour réduire la charge sur le serveur Nagios.

Pour configurer ces différentes méthodes de récupération des métriques dans Nagios, vous devez définir des services et des commandes appropriées. Chaque service spécifie le check à effectuer, et chaque commande définit exactement comment le check est réalisé, y compris l'utilisation d'un plugin spécifique. Ces configurations sont généralement stockées dans des fichiers texte sur le serveur Nagios.

C'est à travers cet ensemble de vérifications actives et passives que Nagios peut surveiller une variété de systèmes backend et recueillir des métriques pour la surveillance de l'état, des performances et de la disponibilité des ressources IT.
Quel plugin utiliser sur Nagios pour récupérer des checks au format d'exposition Prometheus ?

Pour récupérer des checks au format d'exposition Prometheus à partir de Nagios, l'intégration directe n'est pas aussi simple parce que Prometheus et Nagios fonctionnent de manière assez différente pour la collecte de données. Prometheus utilise le modèle de pulling pour recueillir des métriques, tandis que Nagios est basé principalement sur le modèle de pushing pour l'exécution des checks.

Prometheus est conçu pour gratter (scrape) les métriques exposées par des endpoints HTTP. Ces données sont alors stockées dans sa base de données temporelle et sont utilisées pour l'alerting, le monitoring et diverses autres analyses.

Cependant, si vous souhaitez intégrer des données de Prometheus dans Nagios, voici quelques approches que vous pourriez envisager :

1. **Exporter l'état Nagios vers Prometheus :** En utilisant un exportateur qui peut exposer les métriques et l'état de Nagios au format de Prometheus. Un exemple est le `nagios_exporter` qui expose les données de Nagios comme des métriques Prometheus. Les données sont grattées par Prometheus et vous pouvez les utiliser comme d'habitude dans l'écosystème Prometheus.

2. **Exporter les métriques Prometheus vers Nagios :** Si vous voulez effectuer des checks dans Nagios avec les données collectées par Prometheus, vous pouvez écrire ou utiliser un script/plugin custom. Ce script ferait une requête à l'API HTTP de Prometheus pour récupérer la métrique spécifique, la traiterait si nécessaire et la retournerait à Nagios. Gardez à l'esprit que cette intégration ne capitalise pas sur l'approche en temps réel de Prometheus et dépendra des intervalles de checks Nagios.

3. **Prometheus Alertmanager :** Vous pourriez configurer Prometheus pour utiliser Alertmanager pour envoyer des alertes directement à un système de gestion d'incidents ou même de retourner l'information vers Nagios via des checks passifs.

Pour créer ces intégrations, vous auriez besoin d'une bonne compréhension à la fois de Nagios et Prometheus, ainsi que de quelques compétences en programmation pour scripter les intégrations nécessaires.

En résumé, il n'existe pas de plugin out-of-the-box pour intégrer directement les métriques de Prometheus dans Nagios. L'intégration nécessite une certaine personnalisation et dépend beaucoup de vos besoins spécifiques en matière de surveillance et d'alerting.
Peux-tu m'expliquer en détail comment faire pour Exporter les métriques Prometheus vers Nagios ?

Exporter les métriques de Prometheus vers Nagios nécessite une approche où vous récupérez activement les données depuis Prometheus pour les intégrer dans la plateforme de surveillance Nagios. Voici les étapes générales que vous pouvez suivre pour mettre en œuvre cette intégration :

1. **Comprendre les métriques Prometheus à exporter :** Identifiez les métriques spécifiques que vous souhaitez surveiller dans Nagios en provenance de Prometheus.

2. **Configurer Prometheus pour exposer les métriques :** Assurez-vous que Prometheus est configuré correctement pour exposer les métriques à gratter (scrape) à partir de ses targets et que l'accès à l'API HTTP de Prometheus est sécurisé mais disponible pour Nagios.

3. **Créer un plugin Nagios :** Écrivez un plugin Nagios ou un script qui peut interroger l'API HTTP de Prometheus pour récupérer les métriques spécifiques. Un script peut être écrit dans un langage comme Python ou Bash. Ce script devra :

   - Interroger l'API Prometheus pour récupérer des métriques.
   - Traiter la réponse pour extraire la métrique d'intérêt.
   - Convertir les données en un format que Nagios peut comprendre (généralement en retournant un statut OK, WARNING, CRITICAL ou UNKNOWN).
   
   Voici un exemple de base en pseudo-code pour un script écrit en Python :

   ```python
   import requests
   
   # URL de l'API Prometheus où les métriques sont exposées
   prometheus_url = 'http://prometheus_server:9090/api/v1/query'

   # Requête PromQL pour obtenir la métrique désirée
   query = 'some_query{label="value"}'

   # Faites une requête à Prometheus
   response = requests.get(prometheus_url, params={'query': query})
   
   # Traitez la réponse pour obtenir la valeur de la métrique
   if response.status_code == 200:
       result = response.json()['data']['result']
   ```

“${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/application/src/main.cpp”) , will it compile this file without specifiying anything else?

In a CMakeLists.txt file, setting a variable to specify source files, as in your example, doesn't automatically trigger the compilation of those files. You need to explicitly use those variables with commands that define targets, such as `add_executable()` or `add_library()`, for the specified sources to be compiled.

Given your example:
```cmake
set(source "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/application/src/main.cpp")
```

You would then need to create an executable target (for example) using the `add_executable()` command and specify the source variable you've just defined:

```cmake
add_executable(MyApp ${source})
```

This tells CMake to create an executable named `MyApp` using the source file specified in your `source` variable.

Here's a more complete example of a CMakeLists.txt file that incorporates the declaration of the source variable and the creation of an executable:

```cmake
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.10)

# Set the project name and version
project(MyProject VERSION 1.0)

# Specify the C++ standard
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 11)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED True)

# Add a sources variable with your source file
# Assuming your directory structure is something like:
# MyProject/
# |-- application/
#     |-- src/
#         |-- main.cpp
# |-- CMakeLists.txt
set(source "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/application/src/main.cpp")

# Add an executable with the above source
add_executable(MyApp ${source})
```

Note: The above example assumes a directory structure where your `CMakeLists.txt` is located one directory level above your `application/src/main.cpp` file. Adjust the paths as necessary for your project's structure.

So, to summarize, simply setting a variable with a source file path won't compile that file automatically. You need to use commands like `add_executable()` or `add_library()` and specify your variable with the source files to actually compile them into an executable or library.

## 第一章：概述柔性材料

柔性材料是指那些能够在外力作用下容易弯曲、折叠，并且在移除外力后能恢复原状的材料。这类材料在现代工业和科技领域有着广泛的应用。本章将对柔性材料的定义与分类、与刚性材料的对比，以及其发展历程和趋势进行简要介绍。

### 1.1 柔性材料的定义和分类

柔性材料是一大类具有高灵活性和弯曲性的材料，通过其优异的物理特性，它们能够在受到力的作用时发生形变，并且在卸载后能够迅速恢复到原始形状。柔性材料的分类非常广泛，包括但不限于以下几类：

- **塑料（Polymers）**：如聚乙烯、聚丙烯等，具有良好的加工性和成形性。
- **橡胶（Elastomers）**：具有极佳的弹性和耐久性，常见如天然橡胶和各种合成橡胶。
- **织物（Textiles）**：如棉、麻、丝绸等天然纤维和尼龙、涤纶等合成纤维。
- **纳米材料（Nano-materials）**：如碳纳米管、石墨烯等，这些具有特定结构的微观尺度材料赋予了它们独特的灵活性和力学性能。

### 1.2 柔性与刚性材料对比

柔性材料与刚性材料在物理和化学性质上存在显著的差异：

- **弹性模量**：柔性材料一般具有较低的弹性模量，这使得它们在受到相同力的作用时产生较大的形变。
- **折叠和卷曲能力**：刚性材料通常无法在不损坏的情况下进行有效折叠或卷曲，而柔性材料可以轻易进行这样的操作。
- **韧性**：柔性材料在受到撕裂或拉伸时表现出更好的韧性，能够承受更大的应变而不断裂。
- **重量**：相较于大多数刚性材料，柔性材料通常具有更轻的重量，这在需要减轻结构重量的应用中非常有价值。

考虑到它们化学的差异性，柔性材料通常在化学稳定性、耐腐蚀性等方面与刚性材料不同，这直接影响了它们的应用范围和寿命。

### 1.3 发展历程和趋势

柔性材料的研究和应用可以追溯到数千年前，而随着人类对材料性能的深入了解，这些材料的使用也日益普及。从早期简单的使用到如今的高科技领域，柔性材料的发展经历了巨大的变革。

在19世纪末到20世纪初，合成聚合物的发明为柔性材料的发展提供了技术基础。随后，各种合成橡胶和塑料的研究与开发进一步推动了柔性材料科学的进步。

进入21世纪，随着科技的发展，柔性电子技术成为研究的热点，这直接促进了新一代柔性材料如导电高分子、柔性纳米复合材料的出现。它们在可穿戴设备、柔性显示屏、电子皮肤、生物医学工程等领域展现了巨大的应用潜力。

未来发展趋势预计将集中在提高材料性能、拓宽应用范围以及实现环境友好型的可持续发展上。随着材料科学与工程技术的进一步融合，新材料的研发将不断推动社会和工业的进步。同时，对资源回收与绿色制造的重视，将促进环保型柔性材料的研究和应用。
柔性材料与刚性材料在物理和化学性质上存在显著的差异：

柔性材料与刚性材料在物理和化学性质上的区别主要体现在以下几个方面：

1. **物理性质差异**：
   - **弹性模量**：柔性材料通常具有较低的弹性模量，这意味着它们在力的作用下更易发生形变，并能在撤去力后恢复原状。相比之下，刚性材料有较高的弹性模量，对于形变的反应较小。
   - **延展性与韧性**：柔性材料往往拥有高延展性和韧性，能在不断裂的情况下承受较大的形变。刚性材料通常延展性较差，承受大形变时容易发生断裂。
   - **密度**：柔性材料如塑料和橡胶，密度一般较低，重量轻。刚性材料，特别是金属和陶瓷，密度相对较高。
   - **耐疲劳性**：柔性材料能经受重复应力或变形而不发生损坏。刚性材料对于疲劳的抵抗能力相对较弱。

2. **化学性质差异**：
   - **化学稳定性**：柔性材料和刚性材料按其化学组成和结构的不同，表现出不同的化学稳定性。例如，有些塑料和橡胶可能较易受到化学物质（如溶剂、酸、碱）的影响，而金属则可能面临氧化（如生锈）的问题。
   - **耐温性**：不同材料的耐高温和耐低温能力不同。某些塑料在高温下会变形或分解，而某些刚性材料如金属和陶瓷可以在更高的温度下保持性能。
   - **耐腐蚀性**：这表征材料抵抗环境（如湿气、化学品、盐雾）引起的损坏能力，不同材料有不同的耐腐蚀性。例如，不锈钢的耐腐蚀性较好，而普通钢则不然。

综合考虑这些物理和化学性质上的差别，柔性材料和刚性材料在设计和应用上会有很大不同。产品设计师和工程师需要根据最终产品的用途和要求来选择合适的材料类型。

## 第二章：柔性材料的性能要求

为了满足各种应用场景的需求，柔性材料必须具备一定的性能要求，以确保其在使用过程中能保持必要的物理特性和功能性。本章主要探讨这些性能要求，包括机械性能、耐环境性能以及电气性能。

### 2.1 机械性能

柔性材料的机械性能是其最为重要的性能之一，影响着材料的可靠性和实用性。

#### 弱点：
- **撕裂强度**：柔性材料容易因内部缺陷或边缘不规则而起始撕裂。
- **耐磨性**：在反复摩擦或接触其他物体的情况下，柔性材料可能容易磨损。
- **疲劳寿命**：反复应力（如弯曲、折叠）可能导致材料性能下降。

#### 关键性能指标：
- **拉伸强度**：材料在拉伸应力作用下抵抗破坏的能力。
- **伸长率**：材料拉伸至断裂前的最大伸长程度，用以衡量材料的延展性。
- **弹性模量**：描述材料刚度的指标，较低的弹性模量可赋予材料良好的柔性。
- **回弹性**：材料在受到变形后能自行恢复原始形状的能力。

### 2.2 耐环境性能

耐环境性能指材料在各种环境条件下能保持性能不变的能力，这对于确保柔性材料的可靠性和寿命至关重要。

#### 温度、湿度和化学品的影响：
- **耐温性**：柔性材料应能在特定温度范围内维持机械和化学稳定性。
- **耐湿性**：材料要能在高湿环境下保持其物理性能，不发生水解或膨胀等现象。
- **耐化学性**：柔性材料要能抵抗各种化学品的侵害，包括酸、碱、溶剂等。
- **抗紫外线（UV）能力**：对于可能暴露于紫外线下的应用，材料需有良好的耐UV性。

### 2.3 电气性能

对于那些在电气设备中应用的柔性材料，如柔性电路板、传感器、触摸屏等，它们的电气性能同样重要。

#### 导电、绝缘和半导体柔性材料：
- **导电性**：导电性柔性材料，如金属箔或导电聚合物，要求有低电阻率，以保持良好的电流传输效率。
- **绝缘性**：作为绝缘体，柔性材料应具有高的电阻率和良好的介电强度，确保电气隔离。
- **透明电极**：在柔性显示屏等领域，对柔性材料既要求导电性也要求透明度，如铟锡氧化物（ITO）。
- **耐电压性和介电常数**：柔性基板材料需具备一定的耐电压能力，并具有合适的介电常数以满足不同应用需求。

综合而言，柔性材料的性能要求取决于其应用环境和功能需要，选择和设计这类材料需要综合考虑多方面的性能参数，确保材料在实际应用中的长期稳定性和可靠性。

Чтобы код возвращал реальные предсказания модели, вот как это можно реализовать в структуре класса `Classifier`. В этом примере я буду использовать PyTorch для вычисления:

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForSequenceClassification, AutoTokenizer
import torch
from typing import List, Dict

class Classifier:

    def __init__(self, model_path: str) -> None:
        self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_path)
        self.model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(model_path)
        self.model.eval()  # Устанавливаем модель в режим оценки

    def predict(self, texts: List[str]) -> List[List[Dict[str, float]]]:
        outputs = []

        with torch.no_grad(): # Для предсказания градиенты не нужны
            for text in texts:
                inputs = self.tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", padding=True, truncation=True, max_length=512)
                logits = self.model(**inputs).logits
                softmax_logits = torch.softmax(logits, dim=1)
                predictions = softmax_logits.tolist()[0]  # Превращаем в список и берем первый элемент, т.к. это один пример

                # Собираем результаты в нужном формате
                output = []
                for i, score in enumerate(predictions):
                    output.append({"name": f"class_{i+1}", "score": score})

                outputs.append(output)

        return outputs

# Пример использования
model_path = "path_to_your_model"
texts = ["Your text here"]
classifier = Classifier(model_path)
predictions = classifier.predict(texts)

print(predictions)
```

Этот код загружает модель и токенизатор из указанного пути, а затем предсказывает классы для предоставленного текста. В функции `predict`, он принимает список строк (`texts`), каждая из которых предсказывается отдельно. Для каждого текста, он сначала токенизирует текст, а затем подает его на вход модели для получения логитов. После чего применяется функция `softmax`, чтобы преобразовать логиты в вероятности принадлежности к классам. В итоге, функция возвращает список словарей с именами классов и соответствующими вероятностями каждого из них.

Мне нужен способ получения предсказания для мультилейбловой классификации

Для мультилейбловой (мультиклассовой) классификации, где каждый объект может принадлежать к более чем одному классу одновременно, предсказания обычно делаются путем применения функции активации, например, сигмоида, к выходам модели для каждого класса. Это позволяет интерпретировать выход каждого класса как независимую вероятность принадлежности объекта к каждому из классов, что отличает ее от функции softmax, используемой в задачах многоклассовой классификации, где объект может принадлежать только одному классу.

Предположим, что у вас есть предсказание модели в форме тензора, где каждый элемент тензора - это логит предсказания для каждого класса объекта. Ваша задача - преобразовать эти логиты в вероятности.

### Пример

1. **Импортируйте необходимые библиотеки**:

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
```

2. **Определите логиты предсказания**:

Представим, что у вас есть вывод модели (логиты) для одного объекта и трех классов:

```python
logits = torch.tensor([[2.0, -1.0, 0.1]])
```

3. **Примените сигмоидальную функцию активации**:

```python
probabilities = torch.sigmoid(logits)
print(probabilities)
```

Это преобразует каждый логит в значение от 0 до 1, которое можно интерпретировать как вероятность.

4. **Определите порог для классификации**:

Как правило, используется пороговое значение (например, 0.5) для определения, относится ли объект к классу. 

```python
threshold = 0.5
predictions = (probabilities > threshold).long() # Получаем 0 или 1 для каждого класса
print(predictions)
```

5. **Интерпретируйте результаты**:

Если ваш результат выглядит как `[[1, 0, 1]]`, это означает, что объект принадлежит к первому и третьему классам, но не к второму.

Cheng Xiang was eager for the situation to escalate. Although they were all strangers, the prospect of humiliating Jiang Xi was enough to disgust her; seeing Jiang Xi thwarted was, for her, a supreme delight.

Surrounding sales associates and clusters of customers who overheard some gossip watched from a respectful distance.

Lin Xiyue's cheeks were flushed with anger.

Jiang Xi looked at Cheng Xiang with calm and asked, "Cheng Xiang, time and again you push the boundaries of my patience. Do you think I'm that easy to bully?"

"Isn't that the case?" Cheng Xiang scoffed. "Or perhaps you hope your sugar daddy will fight your battles for you? Come on then, let's see what he can do to me!"

Jiang Xi's sugar daddy could never surpass the might of her, Cheng Xiang's, family!

"What's going on here?"

The sudden question interrupted the two women.

Cheng Xiang turned to see who had spoken—Jiang Qiaoqiao? Why was she here?

Beside her stood her fiancé, Duan Youshen.

Jiang Xi saw them too.

Blinking innocently, Jiang Qiaoqiao asked, "Xi Xi, what are you doing here? Having a disagreement with classmate Cheng Xiang again?"

With that word "again," she deftly placed the blame on Jiang Xi.

Cheng Xiang remained defiant, playing with her hair, and said, "Jiang Qiaoqiao, this matter does not concern you. This is an old grudge between us."

She always targeted the person, not the issue.

She didn't want to offend Jiang Qiaoqiao, whose fiancé was not to be trifled with.

Jiang Qiaoqiao, addressing Cheng Xiang with gentleness, said, "Classmate Cheng, as Jiang Xi's sister, if she has done something wrong, I apologize on her behalf. Can we possibly de-escalate this situation, especially with so many onlookers?"

Was the rumor true? Was Jiang Qiaoqiao actually Jiang Xi's sister?

"She is the one lacking decorum, engaging with men indiscriminately. Today, she even fought with me over the same suit. Does the Jiang family's upbringing vary so much from person to person? You, excelling in every aspect, and your sister..."

Her unfinished sentence and expression said it all; it was an attack on one's very heart.

Jiang Xi's pale expression and hoarse voice retorted, "Get it straight—she's not my sister, and I have nothing to do with her. Cheng Xiang, no matter what you do, Wei Jinxue will never give you a second glance. Is any of this worthwhile?"

In revealing her truth, Jiang Xi was also playing a mind game.

Sure enough, at the mention of Wei Jinxue, Cheng Xiang's complexion shifted.

Unable to restrain her temper, she raised her hand, intent on slapping Jiang Xi.

But Jiang Xi caught the hand mid-air.

"Are you angered into a rage? It's fine when you slander others for clinging to power, but become furious over a single truth about yourself? The more enraged you become, does it not indicate the truth in my words?" Jiang Xi shook off Cheng Xiang's hand, feeling as if a great weight had been lifted from her as well.

Jiang Qiaoqiao frowned at her brashness.

Jiang Xi was detestable! After escaping that night, now Mr. Wang was in the ICU, and the Wang family was causing trouble for hers. And here she was, trying to charm other men?

"When will you ever grow up, Xi Xi?" lamented Jiang Qiaoqiao, tired and overwhelmed as more onlookers gathered. "You can disown me as your sister if you wish. But why do you persist in upsetting our father? Why chase after men when our mother is in the hospital, and you should be visiting her instead of indulging in frivolities?"

Her words plunged Jiang Xi deeper into the abyss, as the surrounding crowd murmured against her.

Duan Youshen, witnessing the scene, his handsome face betraying a hint of displeasure, said, "Qiaoqiao, since she does not respect you, there's no need to concern yourself with her fate."

"Mr. Duan, could you please take your beloved fiancée and leave? Your presence here is unwarranted," Jiang Xi retorted without a trace of respect for anyone associated with the Jiang family.

In Duan Youshen's eyes, Jiang Xi lacked sophistication, unlike the cultivated Jiang Qiaoqiao, whom he was engaged to.

A frown crossed his face as he dismissed the thought, for there was no room for "if."

2. **Connection Pool 오류**: 데이터베이스 연결 풀 관련 설정이 잘못되었거나, 데이터베이스 서버 문제로 인해 발생합니다. connection pool 설정을 재검토하고, 데이터베이스 서버가 정상적으로 작동 중인지 확인합니다.

3. **메모리 누수 (Memory Leak)**: JEUS 서버 운영 중 메모리 사용량이 점진적으로 증가하여 서버 성능 저하 또는 강제 종료로 이어지는 문제입니다. 애플리케이션의 코드 리뷰를 통해 메모리 누수 가능성이 있는 부분을 체크하고, 가능한 경우 Java Virtual Machine(JVM)의 메모리 설정을 조정합니다.

Kapitel 1: Der Beginn einer eindrucksvollen Karriere

Der Schreibstil von Tana French ist in hohem Maße von ihrem Hintergrund als Schauspielerin und ihrem Studium der englischen und irischen Literatur geprägt. Why there are so many bizarre things going on in Florida

The notion that "so many bizarre things" happen in Florida is, in part, due to a mix of actual unique conditions of the state and a phenomenon known as the "Florida Man" meme, which has been perpetuated by the media and internet culture. There are several reasons contributing to Florida's reputation for strange and unusual news:

1. **Florida's Sunshine Law**: One of the biggest reasons for Florida's reputation is its very broad public records laws, often referred to as the "Sunshine Law." This law makes it easier for journalists and the public to access government documents and records, including arrest reports. As a result, the activities of Florida residents, especially criminal cases, are more transparent and accessible than in other states, leading to a multitude of news stories.

2. **Population Diversity**: Florida is the third-most populous state in the U.S., with a very diverse population. This includes a large number of retirees, immigrants from different countries, and people from various socioeconomic backgrounds, all mixed together. Diverse populations can mean a wide array of behaviors and thus a broad spectrum of news stories, both ordinary and strange.

3. **Transience**: The state has a transient population, with many people moving in and out. This can contribute to unstable community structures and a higher potential for unusual occurrences as people with various backgrounds and intentions come together.

4. **Tourism**: Florida is one of the top tourist destinations in the world, famous for its beaches, theme parks, and warm climate. This high volume of visitors from all over the globe might contribute to the frequency of odd events, as large groups of people are always coming and going.

5. **Climate**: The warm weather and long summers contribute to an active outdoor lifestyle year-round, which can lead to an increase in the chances of bizarre incidents occurring in public spaces.

6. **Wildlife**: Florida's unique ecosystem is full of a variety of wildlife, including alligators, snakes, and panthers, which sometimes leads to unexpected human-animal encounters that can make for strange headlines.

7. **Media Attention**: Once the "Florida Man" idea took hold, there's been a sort of self-perpetuating cycle where the media is more attuned to reporting on weird events from Florida, thereby reinforcing the stereotype.

It's important to note that weird and unusual events occur in all states and countries, but the combination of factors listed above has contributed to the prominence of Florida's odd happenings in the news. Additionally, not everything coming out of Florida is bizarre or weird; the focus on such news can overshadow the state's many positive stories, achievements, and contributions to culture, science, and the arts.

Judul: Pengaruh Digitalisasi Terhadap Dunia Pendidikan di Era Modern

Pendahuluan:
Perkembangan teknologi informasi dan komunikasi telah menciptakan era baru dalam berbagai aspek kehidupan, termasuk dunia pendidikan. Digitalisasi, yang merupakan proses penggunaan teknologi digital untuk mengubah layanan atau bisnis, telah mengubah cara kita mengakses, mengelola, dan menyampaikan pendidikan. Era modern telah memberikan peluang dan tantangan yang signifikan bagi institusi pendidikan, guru, dan siswa. Artikel ini akan membahas pengaruh digitalisasi terhadap dunia pendidikan dan bagaimana hal ini membentuk masa depan pembelajaran.

Isi:
1. Akses Pendidikan yang Lebih Luas
Digitalisasi telah menyebabkan terciptanya platform e-learning dan kursus online yang memungkinkan siswa dari seluruh dunia untuk mengakses materi pendidikan tanpa batasan geografis. Ini membuka peluang bagi mereka yang sebelumnya tidak dapat menghadiri perkuliahan tradisional karena alasan finansial, geografis, atau waktu.

2. Personalisasi Pembelajaran
Teknologi digital menyediakan data yang berlimpah dan alat analitik yang memungkinkan pendidik memahami kebutuhan belajar unik setiap siswa. Dengan adanya sistem pembelajaran yang adaptif, konten dapat disesuaikan agar lebih relevan dengan kecepatan dan gaya belajar individu, sehingga meningkatkan efektivitas pendidikan.

3. Kerjasama dan Pembelajaran Kolaboratif
Alat digital seperti forum online, media sosial, dan aplikasi kolaborasi telah memfasilitasi komunikasi dan kerja sama antara siswa dan guru dari berbagai belahan dunia. Ini mendorong pertukaran ilmu dan budaya, serta mengembangkan keterampilan seperti kerja tim dan komunikasi antarbudaya.

4. Penggunaan Teknologi Kreatif di Kelas
Dari realitas virtual (VR) hingga kecerdasan buatan (AI), teknologi baru secara aktif digunakan dalam kelas untuk menciptakan pengalaman belajar yang lebih interaktif dan menarik. Simulasi dan game edukatif mendorong keterlibatan siswa dan membantu memperkuat konsep-konsep dengan cara yang menyenangkan.

5. Tantangan Digitalisasi
Meskipun terdapat banyak keunggulan, digitalisasi di dunia pendidikan juga memiliki tantangan. Isu seperti kesenjangan digital, di mana tidak semua siswa memiliki akses yang sama ke teknologi, merupakan salah satu hambatan. Hal ini membutuhkan intervensi untuk memastikan bahwa semua siswa memiliki kesempatan yang sama untuk memanfaatkan teknologi dalam pembelajaran.

6. Persiapan Untuk Dunia Kerja yang Digital
Pendidikan di era modern harus mempersiapkan siswa tidak hanya dengan pengetahuan akademik tetapi juga dengan keterampilan digital yang dibutuhkan di tempat kerja masa depan. Как правильно организовать именование веток в git, распиши подробнее и с примерами

Организация именования веток в Git имеет огромное значение для облегчения работы с кодом и повышения производительности разработчиков. Ниже приведены рекомендации по организации именования веток с примерами.

1. Используйте короткие, но содержательные имена веток.
При выборе имени ветки выбирайте такое имя, которое бы кратко и четко описывало суть вносимых изменений.

Пример: 
- Плохо: `fix` или `new_feature`
- Хорошо: `fix_login_bug` или `add_user_registration`

2. Используйте разделители слов.
В именах веток желательно использовать дефис (`-`), нижнее подчеркивание (`_`) или слэш (`/`) в качестве разделителя слов, чтобы увеличить читаемость имени.

Пример:
- `fix-login-bug`
- `add_user_registration`
- `feature/new-feature`

3. Следуйте общепринятой структуре именования.
Ниже приведена распространенная структура для именования веток:

- `feature/name` - для новых функций
- `fix/name` - для исправления ошибок
- `hotfix/name` - для срочных исправлений 
- `release/name` - для релизных веток
- `chore/name` - для небольших улучшений кода, не связанных с новыми функциями и исправлениями

Пример:
- `feature/user-registration`
- `fix/login-bug`
- `hotfix/security-issue`
- `release/v1.2.1`
- `chore/code-refactoring`

4. Включите идентификатор задачи или проблемы в имя ветки.
Если в вашем проекте используется система трекера задач или проблем (issue tracker), включите идентификатор задачи в имя ветки. Это помогает упорядочить историю изменений и облегчает поиск работы, связанной с конкретной задачей или проблемой.

Пример:
- `feature/ISSUE-123-user-registration`
- `fix/ISSUE-456-login-bug`

Следuющим эффективным подходом к именованию веток является использование правил GitFlow или GitHub Flow, которые предоставляют структурированную модель разработки.

Итак, следуя вышеуказанным рекомендациям, вы сможете внедрить систематический и организованный подход к именованию веток Git. Это поможет вашей команде работать более продуктивно и упростить процесс обновления кода.
А нужно ли указывать версию в названии веток? Как понять к какой версии относится ветка?

Указывать версию в названии веток не является обязательным, но это может быть полезным для определенных случаев. В основном, версии могут использоваться в названиях веток, связанных с релизами, горячими исправлениями или в ветках поддержки для старых версий продукта. 

Добавление версии в название ветки помогает отслеживать изменения, относящиеся к определенным релизам, и упрощает координацию между разработчиками. Оно должно быть согласовано с вашей командой и использоваться согласно общим правилам.

Примеры версий в названиях веток:

1. Релизные ветки:
   - `release/1.0`
   - `release/1.1`
   - `release/2.0`

2. Горячие исправления:
   - `hotfix/1.0.1`
   - `hotfix/1.1.1`
   - `hotfix/2.0.1`

3. Ветки поддержки (для поддержки старых версий продукта с исправлениями и улучшениями):
   - `support/1.x`
   - `support/2.x`

Как понять к какой версии относится ветка:

1. Если версия указана в названии ветки, вы можете определить версию на основе этого. Например, `release/1.0` относится к версии `1.0`.

2. Если версия не указана в названии ветки, вы можете проверить историю изменений, теги и комментарии к коммитам, связанные с данной веткой. Теги часто используются для маркировки состояний репозитория, связанных с определенными релизами. Используйте команду `git tag --list` для просмотра списка тегов и `git show <tag_name>` для детальной информации о теге. Вы также можете использовать `git log <branch_name>` для просмотра истории коммитов и комментариев в этой ветке, которые могут содержать информацию о версии.

3. Уточните у коллег-разработчиков, если информация о версии не является ясной из названия ветки или истории изменений. Рекомендуется использовать хорошо документированный подход к именованию веток и релизов, чтобы избежать путаницы с версиями.
А чем отличаются релизные ветки от обычных?

Релизные ветки (release branches) имеют специфическую цель и используются для подготовки и сопровождения новых выпусков продукта в рамках различных ветвлений и рабочих процессов, таких как GitFlow или GitHub Flow. Вот основные отличия релизных веток от обычных (feature, fix, hotfix, develop и master и др.):

1. Цель релизных веток:
   Релизные ветки создаются с целью подготовки и тестирования новых версий продукта перед их выпуском. Они используются для финальной интеграции всех завершенных функциональностей и исправлений ошибок, последующего тестирования, исправления найденных проблем и применения любых других мероприятий для устранения проблем перед релизом.

2. Происхождение релизных веток:
   Релизные ветки обычно создаются от ветки `develop` или другой основной ветки, когда команда решает, что большинство новых функциональностей и исправлений будут включены в следующий релиз. В процессе подготовки релиза этой ветке могут быть добавлены дополнительные исправления и улучшения.

3. Срок жизни релизных веток:
   Релизные ветки имеют временный характер, поскольку они существуют только в процессе подготовки и выпуска определенной версии продукта. После успешного релиза, релизная ветка сливается в основные ветки (например, `master` и `develop`) и удалается.

4. Взаимодействие с другими ветками:
   В рамках GitFlow, релизная ветка обычно сливается в `master` с присвоением тега версии и в `develop` для включения всех исправлений и изменений, сделанных в процессе подготовки релиза. Это гарантирует, что все изменения, сделанные в релизных ветках, будут применены в будущих релизах.

5. Ограничения на изменения:
   В релизных ветках обычно допускается вносить только те изменения, которые напрямую связаны с подготовкой и выпуском новой версии продукта. Новые функциональности или значительные изменения кода, которые могут вноситься в обычные ветки, стараются избегать в релизных ветках, чтобы не сорвать сроки выпуска.

В целом, релизные ветки служат для изоляции процесса подготовки и выпуска новой версии продукта от параллельно идущей разработки, что обеспечивает стабильность и контроль над изменениями, применяемыми в рамках каждого релиза.
What Specs Would An £4,750 Laptop From 1997 Have?

If you were to purchase a high-end laptop in 1997 for £4,750, which would have been a considerable sum of money for a laptop at the time, you could expect state-of-the-art specifications for that period. While specs would vary depending on the manufacturer and the model, the following are some general specifications that a laptop in that price range might have featured:

1. **Processor**: The CPU would likely be an Intel Pentium or Pentium II, possibly at speeds ranging from 120 MHz to 233 MHz. Some models might feature AMD or Cyrix processors, which were also popular at the time.

2. **Memory (RAM)**: High-end laptops in 1997 would likely come with between 16 MB to 32 MB of RAM, possibly expandable to 64 MB or more.

3. **Storage**: Hard drives were much smaller in capacity and slower than today's SSDs. A premium laptop might come with a 2 GB to 4 GB hard disk drive.

4. **Display**: The display would be an LCD with a resolution that might be around 800x600 or 1024x768 pixels. Color displays with passive or active matrix technology were common, with the better and more expensive models featuring active matrix for sharper images.

5. **Graphics**: Integrated graphics would be the norm, capable of handling basic tasks and some light gaming. Dedicated GPUs were not common in laptops until later.

6. **Optical Drive**: A CD-ROM drive would be common, and a more expensive model might include a DVD-ROM drive, though DVD technology was just emerging at the time.

7. **Ports**: You would expect serial ports, a parallel port for printers, a VGA port for an external monitor, perhaps a PS/2 port for a mouse or keyboard, and maybe one or two PCMCIA slots for expansion cards.

8. **Modem**: Some high-end laptops might include a built-in modem for dial-up internet access, often with speeds of 28.8 or 33.6 Kbps.

9. **Operating System**: It would likely come with Windows 95 or the then-recently released Windows 98. Some may offer Windows NT for a more business-oriented approach.

10. **Battery Life**: Battery technology was much less advanced, with NiMH or NiCd batteries offering perhaps 2-3 hours of battery life, less with heavy usage.

11. **Weight and Size**: Laptops from this era were much bulkier and heavier than modern ultrabooks, possibly weighing 6-10 pounds (about 2.7-4.5 kg) or more.

12. **Extras**: A laptop in this price range might also have included a docking station, additional batteries, or expanded warranty/service plans.

Keep in mind that technology prices drop rapidly as new technology becomes available, so some of the above specifications might have been found in more affordable laptops in the years following 1997. High-end models might also boast brand-specific features, like IBM's ThinkPad line with its iconic TrackPoint, or unique form factors like the early tablets or convertibles (e.g., the Toshiba Portege line).

could you please show me step by step how to scrape the last 100 tweets from the query Counter Strike 2 and save the result to a csv file please and without using the twitter API at all or tweepy thank you

To scrape the last 100 tweets from a query "Counter Strike 2" and save the result to a CSV file without using the Twitter API or Tweepy, you can use a Python library called BeautifulSoup, along with the Requests library. This method involves scraping the Twitter HTML directly, which is slower and less reliable. Here is a step-by-step guide:

1. Install Python libraries BeautifulSoup and Requests
```
pip install beautifulsoup4
pip install requests
```

2. Create a new Python script and import the required libraries.

```python
import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import csv
```

3. Define a helper function for generating a Twitter URL based on the search query and pagination.

```python
def generate_url(query, last_tweets_url=None):
    base_url = 'https://mobile.twitter.com/search?q='
    if last_tweets_url:
        url = base_url + f'"{query}"&count=100&max_id=0&since_id={last_tweets_url}'
    else:
        url = base_url + f'"{query}"&count=100'
    return url
```

4. Define a helper function to parse the Twitter page's HTML for tweet information.

```python
def parse_tweets(soup):
    tweets = []
    tweet_divs = soup.find_all("div", class_="tweet-text")
    for div in tweet_divs:
        tweets.append(div.text.strip())
    return tweets
```

5. Define a function to save the list of tweets to a CSV file.

```python
def save_to_csv(tweets, filename='tweets.csv'):
    with open(filename, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='') as f:
        csv_writer = csv.writer(f)
        csv_writer.writerow(['Tweet'])
        for tweet in tweets:
            csv_writer.writerow([tweet])
```

6. Write a main function to handle the scraping process and saving to a CSV file.

```python
def main(query, max_tweets=100):
    last_tweets_url = None
    tweets = []

    while len(tweets) < max_tweets:
        url = generate_url(query, last_tweets_url)

        response = requests.get(url)
        
        if response.status_code != 200:
            break
            
        soup = BeautifulSoup(response.text, 'html.parser')
        current_tweets = parse_tweets(soup)
        
        if not current_tweets:
            break
            
        tweets.extend(current_tweets)
        
        last_tweet_id_tag = soup.find("div", {"id": "timeline"}).find_all("div", recursive=False)[-1]
        last_tweets_url = last_tweet_id_tag["data-tweet-id"]
    
    tweets = tweets[:max_tweets]
    save_to_csv(tweets)
```

7. Finally, call the main function with the desired search query.

```python
if __name__ == '__main__':
    main('Counter Strike 2', max_tweets=100)
```

Please note that web scraping Twitter's HTML is less stable and against Twitter's Terms of Service, and your script may stop working if Twitter changes its website structure. Always prefer to work with the official Twitter API.
